# 5 Best Robotics ETFs to Buy in 2026
## What Is the Best Humanoid Robotics ETF?
KOID claims to be the first ETF focused specifically on humanoid robotics.

Roundhill Humanoid Robotics ETF ( [HUMN](https://money.usnews.com/funds/etfs/technology/roundhill-humanoid-robotics-etf/humn)), which started up in the same month and has a one-year return of 36%, also says it's the first of its kind. However, Themes Humanoid Robotics ETF ( [BOTT](https://money.usnews.com/funds/etfs/technology/themes-humanoid-robotics-etf/bott)), up 54% over the past year, has been around a little longer, since 2024. Both HUMN and BOTT allocate about 5% of assets to Tesla Inc. ( [TSLA](https://money.usnews.com/investing/stocks/tsla-tesla-inc)), incidentally, though the automaker and Optimus humanoid robot developer is not the No. 1 holding for any of these funds right now.

Robo Global Robotics & Automation Index ETF( [ROBO](https://money.usnews.com/funds/etfs/technology/robo-global-robotics-automation-etf/robo)), up 37% over the past year, takes a wider view of the robotics market but does focus on physical AI and has been around since 2013.

If you are more interested in taking a flier on a hot upstart ETF, consider one of the aforementioned leaders in humanoid robotics funds:

## Global X Robotics & Artificial Intelligence ETF ( [BOTZ](https://money.usnews.com/funds/etfs/technology/global-x-robotics-artfcl-intllgnc-etf/botz))
BOTZ has a 0.68% expense ratio and is up by 14% over the past year. It is a top robotics fund for investors who want [international exposure](https://money.usnews.com/investing/articles/best-international-stocks-to-buy). Only three of the top 10 holdings are U.S. companies, and a little less than one-third of the portfolio is in domestic stocks. Japanese and Chinese companies make up roughly half of the entire fund. Four of the top five stocks, which include ABB Ltd. (OTC: ABBNY) and Nvidia Corp. ( [NVDA](https://money.usnews.com/investing/stocks/nvda-nvidia-corp)), are up big over the past year.

The fund's portfolio managers have been at the helm for almost a decade, and one of them, Nam To, has a stake in the ETF up to $50,000.

The fund's website also mentions that humanoid robots can be an answer to labor shortages and aging demographics. If that scenario occurs, it can quickly result in booming demand for the technology and may be enough to help this fund reliably [outperform the S&P 500](https://money.usnews.com/investing/articles/etfs-that-outperform-the-s-p-500).

# Robotics ETFs Will Dominate the 2030s. This 1 ETF Is Trading at a Discount
## An under-the-radar pick that is surprisingly diversified
The **KraneShares Global Humanoid Robotics and Physical AI Index ETF ( [NASDAQ:KOID](https://247wallst.com/companies/KOID/?tpid=1626241&tv=link&tc=in_content))** is the first U.S.-listed ETF that is dedicated to humanoid robotics.

This is a much better roster of stocks than that of the most popular robotics ETF, the **Global X Robotics and Artificial Intelligence ETF ( [NASDAQ:BOTZ](https://247wallst.com/companies/BOTZ/?tpid=1626241&tv=link&tc=in_content))**. BOTZ is top-heavy, with its 4 largest holdings accounting for ~36% of the ETF.
